Every sampled HTML page was rendered.

suggested_action.how: Enable the framework's server rendering or static generation for these routes, or put a prerendering step in front of them serving the rendered HTML to every client alike; then confirm with a plain fetch that headings and body text are present.
suggested_action.mechanism: Extraction of the page's text from the fetched response.
suggested_action.success_criteria: A plain fetch with no JavaScript of every cited URL returns the main headings and body text, so that at least a fifth of what the rendered page shows is already in the server response.
suggested_action.summary: Server-render, statically generate or prerender these routes so their text is in the server response.
suggested_action.what: Put the page's substance in the server response for the templates across the site.
suggested_action.where: The routes cited and the rendering configuration of their templates.
suggested_action.why: Text assembled in the browser does not exist for a fetcher that does not run scripts.

findings.evidence: 4 of 4 non-root 2xx pages that declare a canonical name http://127.0.0.1:53327/, the site root, as their canonical URL. Each tells an indexer it is a duplicate of the home page.
exceptions_checked: single retired page consolidated into home: at least 2 distinct paths required

suggested_action.how: Generate the href from the request path, or from the router's resolved route in a client-rendered application, and make sure the server response carries the per-page value.
suggested_action.success_criteria: Every cited URL returns a canonical equal to its own final URL in the server response.
suggested_action.summary: Emit a per-page canonical equal to each page's own URL.
suggested_action.what: Make each page's rel=canonical name its own URL.
suggested_action.where: The shared layout, head component or application shell that emits rel=canonical on the URLs cited.
suggested_action.why: A canonical is per-page by definition, so a fixed value in a shared layout declares every page a duplicate of one.

findings.evidence: /llms.txt at http://127.0.0.1:53327 answered HTTP 200 with no file: an empty body or the site's page for unknown addresses, so no /llms.txt is published. No major assistant is documented to read this file, so this is listed only as a low-cost hedge, not as a gap.

suggested_action.how: Write a short markdown file: one paragraph describing the organization, then links to the pages that answer the questions people ask about it. Keep it consistent with those pages.
suggested_action.mechanism: A possible, undocumented discovery channel for tools that adopt the convention.
suggested_action.success_criteria: /llms.txt answers 200 with content that is not the site's soft-404 page.
suggested_action.summary: If it costs little, publish a short /llms.txt; do not expect it to change how assistants see the site.
suggested_action.what: Publish a plain-text /llms.txt summarising what the site is and linking its key pages.
suggested_action.why: It is a proposed convention some tools read; no major assistant documents consuming it, which is why this is a suggestion and never reported as a problem.
